summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, prior pancreas and kidney transplants, and a mechanical mitral valve was admitted with low-grade fever, whole-body pain, and abdominal discomfort following hemodialysis. Initial evaluation revealed an elevated INR of 6.7, which was managed with vitamin K and warfarin dose adjustments. A new left lower lobe infiltrate on chest X-ray prompted treatment with azithromycin for possible pneumonia, despite minimal respiratory symptoms. Abdominal pain was initially concerning for mesenteric ischemia or transplant rejection, but CT angiography showed patent mesenteric vessels and no evidence of ischemia; instead, significant fecal loading supported constipation as the primary cause. Pain was controlled with rectal morphine suppositories, which the patient tolerated well without nausea. The peritoneal dialysis catheter site showed no infection, and cultures were negative. She was discharged home with stable pain, resolved infection concerns, and a plan for close INR monitoring, bowel regimen optimization, and follow-up for a known right adnexal cyst and pleural effusion.
